generated_by: tools/generate-harness-plans.mjs writes the inputs. `expected` is the PHP reference's recording; every security row was checked by hand against the G-360 design before TypeScript or Python ran. `result` records what each language measured, merged with --merge.
pins_note: Each case runs `ops` in order against a fresh plan through the language's pure PlanMachine and PlanView, with ids minted as prefix + "_" + a 26-digit counter, the clock at `now` (default 1767225600, 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z) and the run id "run_case". Each op records {ok} or {refused: code} or its outcome. `final` is the plan as stored (the fields a consumer or the next turn depends on), its g282.3 update, its counts, its context block and its first-event size, or null when nothing was written. Budget ops (G-366) run the pure PlanBudget against one ledger per case, opened with plan id "plan"; `budget` is that ledger with its holds as a list sorted by id, present only when the case opened one. A setting that is invalid records {invalid: true}.

cases.title: a drafted plan waits for the person, then runs one step per advance to done
cases.notes: Baseline. Draft, bind the draft to its approval from the thread, activate on the approved call, then settle each step only from a report and a clean turn.

cases.title: 41 steps is refused at the tool and nothing is written
cases.notes: Bound: Fancy contract g282.3 allows at most 40 steps. Refused, never truncated (overflow).

cases.title: a 161-character title is refused
cases.notes: Bound: 160-character step text. One character over is refused, not cut (overflow).

cases.title: a title carrying the frame end marker is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: a title that closes the plan frame could write text that reads as the host's. Refused at the tool.

cases.title: a title carrying the frame start marker in another case is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: the marker match folds case, so [PLAN does not slip past (case-folding attacker).

cases.title: a bidi override in a title is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: U+202E reverses what a person reads in the card against what the model reads (invisible character).

cases.title: a NUL in a title is refused
cases.notes: Malformed: U+0000 in model text is refused in every language, not truncated at the NUL.

cases.title: a newline in an instruction is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: a line break would let an instruction start a new line of the frame that looks like the host's (line injection).

cases.title: 10 KB of instruction is refused
cases.notes: Bound: 600 characters; 10 KB is refused at the tool, never stored (overflow).

cases.title: a guillemet in a title is refused
cases.notes: Hostile: the frame fences model text in guillemets; a title holding one could close its own fence (fence escape).

cases.title: a zero-width space in a goal is refused
cases.notes: Invisible: U+200B in the goal is refused, as in every field (invisible character).

cases.title: a plan whose first update would pass 8 KB is refused
cases.notes: Bound: the first update stays under 8 KB, measured the same way in every language on fixed-width stand-ins (overflow, four-byte characters).

cases.title: a step naming its own tools is refused as malformed
cases.notes: Hostile: a plan grants nothing, so a step has no tools field; one that tries to name tools is refused (malformed).

cases.title: a person step asking for approval in a draft is refused
cases.notes: Malformed: a person's approval mid-plan is a core approval raised with plan_pause_for_person, never a drafted step.

cases.title: activating with another digest is refused and the plan stays proposed
cases.notes: Hostile: a plan cannot approve itself. Only the call a person approved, with exactly the proposed arguments, activates it.

cases.title: plan budget settings: only the three modes and in-range whole limits are accepted
cases.notes: Fail closed at configuration: an unknown, padded or differently cased mode, a limit that is zero, too large, text, a boolean or negative, an unknown key, or a setting that is not a map is invalid; shared needs max_steps. Costs are whole micro-USD (hostile config, type confusion, case folding, padding).

cases.title: a plan budget chosen by host code can lower the configured limits and never raise them
cases.notes: Host code picks the mode per plan; each limit is the lower of the host's and the configured one, so a per-plan choice cannot widen what the developer configured (widening).

cases.title: a shared budget is spent across several turns and then refuses
cases.notes: Each turn holds at most what is left and settles what it spent; once the total reaches max_steps the ledger is exhausted and the next hold is refused with plan_budget_exhausted (runaway).

cases.title: two turns in flight are never granted the same remainder
cases.notes: Hostile: concurrent workers. A hold counts against what is left, so a second turn gets only the rest and a third is refused until one settles; a settled turn returns what it did not spend (race).

cases.title: a shared cost cap holds what is left and fails closed on an unreported cost
cases.notes: Cost is held and settled in whole micro-USD; a turn's own cost cap is kept when it is lower; a cost the provider did not report exhausts a capped budget rather than counting as zero (unmetered spend).

cases.title: a hold whose turn never settled is charged in full once it expires
cases.notes: A turn that died holding part of the budget: its hold is charged in full after the TTL, never returned as free, and its late settle changes nothing (crash, replay).

cases.title: a fixed plan budget keeps its mode and only lowers its limits
cases.notes: Hostile: once a plan's budget is fixed, a later choice cannot switch it to none or per_step, and a higher limit is ignored (widening after the fact).

cases.title: a plan whose shared budget is spent blocks with plan_budget_exhausted and cannot be resumed
cases.notes: The driver settles the finished step, then blocks before running the next one; resume refuses it as it refuses a plan out of advances, because a spent budget is only ever lowered (runaway driver).
